cards.title: Track and rank product-research candidates
cards.claim: The speaker recommends recording favorite products, competitor pages, buy price, intended selling price, and notes in a Google Sheet, then narrowing daily additions to one product to run.
cards.action: Make a Google Sheet for product candidates; add competitor pages, buy price, intended selling price, and research notes. If adding three products in a day, narrow them to three favorites, choose one favorite, and run that product.
do_not_use_when: A buy price or intended selling price has not been estimated
The product has not been checked against the speaker's stated criteria
unknowns: What the complete product-selection criteria are
Whether this process produces profitable results
evidence_quotes: "do yourself a favor and make a Google sheet where you write down your favorites"
"Maybe you add some competitor pages that you can get back to later."
"You can add the buy price and what you intend on selling it for."
"you can also add some notes like haven't seen it much on on Facebook, for example, but it's on Tik Tok."
"every day let's say you add three products you niche it down to your three favorites and then you pick your one favorite out of the three favorites"
"then you go ahead and run that product"

cards.title: Use competitor targeting gaps to develop audience angles
cards.claim: The speaker recommends researching a product and its competitors to identify audiences or angles competitors are not targeting, rather than marketing the product generically to the same audience.
cards.action: Research the product and competitors, then look for audiences or angles they are not addressing before developing a marketing angle.
applies_when: Competitor ads or product marketing can be reviewed
do_not_use_when: The proposed audience-product fit has not been validated
The product's claims cannot be supported for the proposed audience
unknowns: How to validate an untapped audience
Whether a competitor gap reflects demand rather than lack of demand
How to assess legal or platform-policy limits for targeting and claims
evidence_quotes: "find untapped markets. Okay? And the way that we do this is with our marketing."
"The easiest way to detect market opportunity is by searching up the product on Tik Tok."
"step number one, find a product that solves a problem. Step two, identify blue oceans by researching a product, finding competitors, and seeing what they're not doing."
"if we can show a saturated product to a new audience, we can give it a new life"

cards.title: Review competitor volume and seriousness as a research heuristic
cards.claim: The speaker uses a heuristic of seeking products with no more than 10 selling stores and no more than three serious competitors; inactive sellers and poor-quality stores are treated as less serious competition.
cards.action: When using Magic AI to search a product, review the stores selling it and assess the speaker's stated thresholds for total sellers and serious competitors.
applies_when: Using Magic AI or a comparable competitor-discovery tool
Reviewing a product's active sellers on Facebook
do_not_use_when: Competitor seriousness cannot be assessed reliably from available storefront or activity information
The thresholds are being treated as proven predictors of success
unknowns: Whether the listed competitors represent the full market
evidence_quotes: "our goal here is that no more than 10 stores are selling it and that no more than three are serious competitors."
"he's not a very serious competitor. The store looks absolutely awful."
"what that would mean in this situation is that it's a pretty green flag to start running it."
